implementation_guards: AcceptSync requires promised ballot and Follower/Prepare; incremental AcceptDecide requires Follower/Accept and expected sequence. Decide requires Accept phase and expected sequence.
writes: AcceptSync installs supplied history, decided index and sequence; incremental messages append entries and advance decided index with batching bounds.

implementation_guards: Promise ballot equals leader ballot; distinct promise slots counted toward prepare quorum. Accepted requires current ballot and Leader/Accept.
writes: Choose maximal accepted round/index history; synchronize log; append buffered proposals unless stopped; record accepted indexes and update decided index when acceptance quorum supports it.
external_effects: Queue AcceptSync, AcceptDecide and Decide messages for promised followers.
unknowns: Same-ballot recovery may replace peer support metadata; accepted indexes are assigned rather than max-merged. Consequence depends on permitted message history.

implementation_guards: New leader ballot exceeds remembered leader and promise; follower accepts higher promise or equal promise in Recover.

after.protocol_context: Reconnect, sequence gap or stored promise

external_effects: Periodic resend sends cached Promise in Prepare or PrepareReq in Recover; leader retries prepares for unpromised peers.

formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question.
